relationship: Changing a circle construction changes its measured angles and lengths; the applicable theorem links them only while its geometric conditions remain true.

learnerLoop.action: Repair a diameter or tangent, open a chord, move a point within a segment, or match and rotate a chord; retain separated observations and predict a linked angle or length.
learnerLoop.modelChange: The same local coordinates determine all chords, radii, tangent contacts, angle sectors, perpendicular feet and numerical readings. A broken condition changes the visible geometry and invalidates its test.
learnerLoop.evidence: Live sectors, exact right-angle marks, midpoint ticks, retained dashed constructions and explicit prediction overlays connect the operated model to persistent calculations and structured reasons.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Decide which condition justifies the relationship; revise a prediction or construction, test it again, and compare immutable readings in the open experiment.

invariants: Dependent angles remain governed by the selected circle theorem as the construction moves.
Every calculation is justified by the required geometric conditions and applicable circle theorem.
safeAdaptations: Vary valid circle configurations and angle values while preserving each theorem relationship.
Adjust working requirements or feedback without replacing construction-based evidence.
nonGoals: Treating a visually plausible angle as proof without its circle-theorem reason.

goal.description: One short mission and operation cue above the model and working. The label names the current relationship without a numeric progress counter.

model.description: Circle geometry with shared SVG handles. Sectors and right-angle markers follow the represented points; captions state whether the theorem condition holds.
model.visibility: Always present; only handles relevant to the current decision are available.

working.description: Reference calculations appear after the first observation. Later tasks replace supplied values with numeric entries and, at All, a structured circle-property choice. Wrong numerical predictions draw dashed rays or lengths on the model.
working.visibility: Observations after the first retained reading. Predictions from entry, except paired-tangent working after its comparison. Experiment live working with optional prediction.

ownership.description: None supplies calculations, Some owns the key answer, All also owns applicable intermediate quantities and the circle reason. Changes preserve construction, observations and entries but clear the current test verdict.
ownership.visibility: Prediction steps and experiment; observation-only experiences show worked evidence.

actions.description: The existing discovery dock keeps one primary Keep/Test/Continue action. Visited experiences restore their snapshots. The shared double-click guard prevents an accidental second advance.
actions.visibility: Beside the model on wide layouts and below it on narrow layouts.

help.description: Evidence-first hints and contrasting worked examples are opt-in. Shared quantity keys connect source labels and operands on hover, focus or tap; value tracing runs only on explicit Trace values.
help.visibility: Hints on request in guided work; tracing when visible source/operand pairs exist.

checkpoints.description: Small markers name real experiences. Current revision clears that experience’s checked marker; visited navigation is not new completion. Future details contain names, not answers.

experiment.description: Four continuous construction families, optional prediction, and up to six deep-copied readings. Selected same-family readings draw fixed dashed comparisons. Cross-family records remain textual without invalid overlays.

reset.description: Repeat resets the current experience. Restart uses the existing inline confirmation and clears all snapshots and readings. Cancellation and Escape preserve them.
reset.visibility: Available throughout; shared transitions temporarily disable actions.

completion.description: Completion uses current geometric conditions, separated evidence or manipulation, and checked owned entries. Empty work stays pending; checked mistakes have an x, correct fields a check.
completion.visibility: After the meaningful model operation and required working. Experiment predictions can be checked without ending exploration.

diameter-angles.description: Angles CAB, ACB and ABC in a triangle on the circle. ACB is 90 degrees only when AB passes through O. The transfer sets CAB = 35 degrees and asks for ABC = 55 degrees.
diameter-angles.domain: Degrees. Repair/exploration B: -60 to 45 degrees; C: 65 to 145 degrees. The transfer fixes B and bounds C to 40–145 degrees. Points cannot coincide.
diameter-angles.source: CircleModel point coordinates and vector-angle geometry; shared pointer/keyboard setters.
diameter-angles.output: Live sectors and triangle-sum working; a checked wrong prediction draws an independent dashed ray.

chord-angle-network.description: Non-reflex centre angle AOB, opposite-arc circumference angle ACB, same-segment angle ADB and tangent–chord angle at A.
chord-angle-network.domain: Opening 70–150 degrees. C and D stay on the appropriate major arc, separated in the two-vertex task. Candidate tangent offset 55–120 degrees.
chord-angle-network.source: A at 210 degrees; B is A plus opening. Circle positions and the candidate line determine actual angles and the second intersection.
chord-angle-network.output: Centre/circumference ratio 2, same-segment equality, and alternate-segment equality only after exact tangency.

paired-tangents.description: Radius OA, hypotenuse OP, tangent lengths PA/PB, and complementary angles APO/AOP.
paired-tangents.domain: Guided radius 8 cm, OP 10 cm, PA = PB = 6 cm. Contacts have distinct upper/lower intervals. P rotates -30 to 30 degrees after exact tangencies. Experiment OP/r: 1.1–1.9.
paired-tangents.source: Contacts solve acos(r/OP); length is sqrt(OP squared minus radius squared). Before locking, independent candidate contacts have actual measured corner angles.
paired-tangents.output: Right-angle squares, equal-length ticks, retained pair, linked Pythagorean working, and experimental radius–tangent angle prediction.

chord-distance.description: Full chords AB/CD, half-chords AM/CN, and perpendicular centre distances OM/ON.
chord-distance.domain: Worked case r = 5 cm, AB = 6 cm, OM = 4 cm; moving half-chord 1–4.5 cm. Transfer r = 13 cm, AB = CD = 10 cm, AM = 5 cm, OM = ON = 12 cm. Midpoint orientation 215–325 degrees.
chord-distance.source: Symmetric endpoints and midpoints use one radius and half-chord; distance is sqrt(radius squared minus half-chord squared).
chord-distance.output: Perpendicular marks, bisected-chord ticks, equal-distance comparison and dashed predicted distance.

modes.none: Supplied calculations never replace construction or comparison. Prediction steps still require explicit Test.
modes.some: The key numeric angle or length is required, supported by theorem/setup. Paired tangents require transferred PB.
modes.all: The key answer, applicable intermediate PA or AM, and structured circle reason are required. No keyword or free-text grading.
modes.guided: Eight connected experiences. Diameter, centre-angle and equal-chord observations introduce relationships before prediction tasks.
modes.experiment: Ungated diameter, chord-angle, tangent and chord-distance manipulation with immutable comparisons and optional predictions. No random generator or external runtime requests.

dependencies: Repair AB as a diameter; keep two C positions separated by at least 30 degrees. The first introduces triangle-angle working.
Place C so CAB = 35 degrees. Test ABC and, at All, the semicircle reason.
Keep two chord openings separated by at least 30 degrees; compare centre and circumference angles.
Predict at D and move D at least 30 degrees from its start within the same segment before Test.
Repair the tangent so OA is perpendicular to AT, then test its alternate-segment angle.
Repair two distinct tangent contacts. Keep P positions at least 25 degrees apart with OP fixed, then calculate the tangent lengths.
Match CD to AB and keep two orientations at least 30 degrees apart; compare perpendicular distances.
In the radius 13 cm, chord 10 cm transfer, turn CD at least 30 degrees and predict its hidden perpendicular distance.
Experiment predictions require fresh manipulation and the applicable condition. A broken diameter becomes a counterexample, not an accepted semicircle calculation.
implementation.completion: CircleModel.complete requires current geometry and meaningful manipulation/evidence. Comparisons use separated positions rather than accumulated wiggles. Predictions require explicit Test and every owned field. Geometry, input and support edits clear verdicts; restored snapshots are prior evidence, not new mastery.
limitations: Ideal Euclidean constructions, not a proof engine. Structured reasons check recognition of conditions, not complete written proofs.
Angular snaps within 2.6 degrees produce exact diameter, tangent or stated triangle conditions; chord half-length snaps within 0.11 cm. Right-angle squares appear only at exact geometric conditions.
Readings are shown to one decimal place. Numeric checks allow an absolute tolerance of 0.11 degree or cm; calculations retain full precision.
The centre model deliberately bounds non-reflex angles and the opposite arc. It does not claim reflex-angle or cyclic-quadrilateral coverage.
Accepted paired tangencies are constrained during the P-orbit comparison. The final tangent experiment maintains exact contacts while P moves radially.
Oversized predicted lengths are truncated at the display boundary and labelled as extending beyond view. Invalid angle ranges are labelled instead of drawing plausible sectors.
Records are session-only, limited to six. Repeat restores a fixed authored configuration; no seeded variation is implemented.
The final experiment replaces the former random mixed-practice sequence with consequential continuous changes and optional calculation. Guided completion is not a claim of exam mastery.
